concept.name: Stacked imbalance
concept.definition: A cluster of bid/ask imbalances occurring at several adjacent price levels within the same bar — typically three or more consecutive levels exceeding the imbalance ratio on the same side. It indicates sustained one-sided aggression across a price zone rather than at a single level.
concept.intuition: One lopsided level can be chance; a whole staircase of lopsided levels shows a determined initiative push through a zone.
concept.mechanics: Platforms scan each bar's diagonal bid/ask comparisons and highlight groups where the imbalance condition holds over a configurable number of consecutive levels; stacked buy imbalances near lows are often read as initiative buying, stacked sell imbalances near highs as initiative selling.
concept.failure_modes: Thresholds (ratio, number of levels) are arbitrary platform settings; stacked imbalances occur frequently in fast directional moves and many are immediately retraced, so they mark zones of interest rather than trade signals.
concept.misconceptions: Stacked imbalances are often treated as automatic support/resistance, but they only record where aggression was one-sided; if that aggression is absorbed and price closes through the zone, the levels fail like any other.
concept.example: During a drive off the low, a bar prints buy imbalances at four consecutive ticks; the platform marks a stacked buy imbalance, and the trader watches that zone as a potential pullback reference.

citations.source: Sierra Chart — Numbers Bars (Highlight Multiple Adjacent Bid or Ask Dominant Prices — Stacked Imbalance)
